Procurement asked us to collect a bit more detail on how Redwood Inference would handle the implementation and cutover for a tiered deployment (pilot -> canary -> general availability). Please see the attached spreadsheet (RFP_Q1_implementation_questions.xlsx) — the questions focus on:

- Typical timeline from contract signature to GA for a mid-sized customer (200k monthly requests)
- Integration touchpoints (auth, telemetry, SSO, model catalog sync) and required owners
- Canary criteria (error budget, latency gates, sampling) and switchback procedures
- Shadow/dual-write approaches for data residency and auditability
- Backout windows and restore cadence (config + data)

For context, we have a hard maintenance blackout on weekends (Sat, Sun) except for emergency fixes. Our data residency requirement is US-EAST. Can you fill the spreadsheet and return a proposed runbook and timeline by EOD 22 Mar? We also want to schedule a 45-minute technical review the week after.

Hi Tim / Laura — attaching a draft implementation timeline and runbook (implementation-timeline-draft.pdf). Key excerpts below. Please read and flag anywhere we need to tighten dependencies.

High-level schedule (calendar days after SOW signature):
- Day 0–7: Kickoff, account provisioning (VPC peering, KMS integration), access matrix
- Day 8–21: Integration work (auth, telemetry endpoints, initial model selection and quantization config)
- Day 22–28: Internal smoke tests + pre-production shadowing (10% traffic for sampling)
- Day 29–35: Customer canary — 3 waves: 5% -> 20% -> 50% (48-hour observation windows)
- Day 36+: GA (gradual increase to steady-state traffic)

Canary & acceptance gates (examples):
- Error rate: must remain <= 0.5% above baseline for two consecutive observation windows
- 95p latency: within 1.5x of baseline model
- Quality regressions: measured by canary prompt set (A/B pass rate >= 95%)
- Operational telemetry: token-level spend and KV cache hit rate within expected bounds

Switchback/backout play:
- Automated rollback to previous stable model variant if error threshold trips twice within a 24-hour window
- Route rollback at routing layer and drain in-flight requests (expected < 90s for graceful drain)
- Full config restore from versioned deployment state (artifactized in our registry) — estimated restore time 15–45 minutes (config-only); model cache priming may add additional warm-up (2–6 hours for large KV sets)

Shadowing approach:
- Dual-path delivery (shadow mode) to store both responses and full telemetry to an audit store in your US-EAST residency; no live downstream effect until canary is promoted

Questions for StellaHealth:
1) Do you have a preferred SSO provider (Okta / AzureAD)?
2) Can you accept a short scheduled maintenance slot in the week before GA for final latency tuning (we recommend a 90-minute window on a weekday evening)?

If these assumptions work I'll fold the answers into the final runbook and the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Prioym

Subject: Re: Draft: Implementation timeline & canary criteria (attached)

Prioym / Laura — thanks for the draft. A few clarifications from our side:

- SSO: Okta (SCIM + SAML) is our standard.
- Maintenance window: we cannot commit to evening changes during HIPAA audit week (first week of April). Can you propose an alternative slot?
- Shadowing: we need the audit store to be write-only for your service and encrypted with our customer-managed KMS keys. Any exported telemetry must include request ids and model-version tags.
- Backout expectations: our internal ops require that a full rollback plan includes DB migration cheek-checks; we will not accept more than 2 hours of potential degraded throughput during a backout.

We're broadly aligned with the canaries you listed but need the documentation to call out the DB migration verification step and a tighter warm-up window. Once you incorporate these, we'll move to scheduling the review.

-Natalie

- Capacity: for a 200k/month customer we recommend starting the canary at 10% of projected peak concurrent throughput (not strictly % of requests) — this allows smoother cache priming.
- Support coverage: we can provide a dedicated on-call rotation for the first 30 days of canary for rapid triage (SLA: 30-minute response for Sev-1 during business hours)

Natalie / Tim — attached is the consolidated runbook and the filled spreadsheet (stellahealth-mamp-final.xlsx). Summary of action items and adjustments we made based on your replies: 

1) SSO: Okta (SCIM + SAML) integration steps included (owner: StellaHealth IdP team; Redwood SE will provide service provider metadata).
2) Maintenance windows: proposed weekday evening slot moved to Tue 2026-04-06 20:00–21:30 ET to avoid HIPAA audit week and still allow post-cutover verification.
3) DB migration checks: added explicit pre- and post-migration verification steps and a dry-run validation executed during the pre-production shadowing phase (Day 22–28).
4) Shadowing & encryption: telemetry exported to an audit bucket in US-EAST with envelope encryption using your KMS keys; records include request id and model-tag metadata.
5) Canary gates tightened: warm-up reduced to targeted priming window (expected model cache steady-state within 3–5 hours), and backout TRIP if throughput degrades >20% for two consecutive windows.
6) Commercial: Ben included pilot crediting language; specific numbers are in the attached spreadsheet (pricing appendix).

Next steps:
- Please confirm the maintenance slot by 2026-03-24 and send any additional compliance artifacts you require for KMS integration.
- Proposed technical review: 2026-03-25 (45 minutes). I'll send a calendar invite once we confirm.

Attachments: stellahealth-mamp-final.xlsx

Thanks everyone — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the runbook.

Best,
Laura
